verification_scope_reason: Pure SSH candidate serialization and hosted-Git exclusions plus actual Git commands against a shared local bare repository and loopback HTTP. Checks HTTPS success, SSH-only fallback and failed fallback, cancellation suppressing SSH, readable Git checks, HTTP and authentication failures, URL credential removal from displayed argv, bounded returned output with full retained stderr, total deadline and cancellation, GitHub host gating. Actual Git trace events compare executed read-only arguments. Source and Native use the same git executable, repository and loopback endpoint. Native additionally checks a 200010-byte streamed log, missing Git under an explicit empty PATH, and Task cancellation that waits for both parent and descendant handles to signal exit. Existing package-view and manager-inspection consumers pass. Tests exposed Windows CreateProcess parent-PATH searching and a disposal cancellation race; queries now resolve commands through the runtime using explicit env and directly terminate/join their owned handle before disposing. Structured executable-not-found is folded to ENOENT. GitLab empty project and URL path serialization differences were corrected and paired again.
legal_adaptation: Known hosted-Git HTTP recognition is translated from the pinned dependency rather than importing Node. For cancellation and silent termination, Git/curl/launcher-dependent diagnostic bytes and status are compared as failure/diagnostic presence; timeout text, timeout kind, displayed argv and cancellation/retry behavior remain exact. Streaming logs retain original stderr bytes, with only the requested tail decoded. No install/update transaction or build execution is certified here.
activation_boundary: Read-only Git preflight helpers and owned-query lifecycle only. Current manager installation/update/removal and built-in Python backend composition continue; production release is not promoted.

discarded_output_followup.reason: Executor review found that subprocess output modes expose collect/pipe/inherit, not output-side ignore. Drain discarded streams through zero-byte collectors to avoid filling unread pipes. New process writes 2 MB to each discarded stream, and the full-log case writes 1.4 MB discarded stdout before stderr. Both complete normally. Explicitly close the owned stderr pipe after its worker joins; streaming and process-tree cancellation direct consumers rerun after that final edit.

cleanup.notes: Initial cleanup encountered read-only synthetic Git loose objects. Verified each remaining object's owned path, no reparse point and link count one before clearing only its read-only attribute; all identified test payloads then removed. Earlier partial deletion was not included in reclaimed-byte lower bound. Compact logs/receipts and resolved failure observations retained; shared Source/toolchains remain through C9.
